pages: Grab Grass! Herbivorous cuisine. Salads, root bowls, and our bestseller, the Lawn Wrap. It is a wrap, and it has lawn in it, and people keep buying it.
I'm a mole, so I'm partial to roots, and worms. We keep it vegan up here. What I eat on my break, down the hole, is between me and the hole.
Five generations of Burrowbys dug under Toggleton market. I'm the first working under a ceiling this high. Mum says the light'll ruin my eyes. I tell her it's going slowly.

stock.name: Lawn Wrap
stock.desc: A wrap with lawn in it.

stock.name: Root Bowl
stock.desc: Dug up under the loading dock by Moss himself. He comes back up squinting.

stock.name: Side Salad
stock.desc: Lettuce, plus whatever came up with it. Moss's mum sends the radishes.

stock.name: Selunemas Wreath Wrap
stock.desc: Please don't wear it.

interactables.name: Celestin Mumblequill
pages: Panto's Try! Enchanted variety foods. Soup that sings, bread that bows, a pie that tells a joke. The pie's joke is bad. We're working on it together.
Twenty years I stage-managed a Panto touring troupe. Then the theatres bought a bard automaton that plays all eight parts. Now my cast is lunch, and lunch turns up.
He hums one bar over a bowl, and the steam rises like a curtain. 'An old cue from my prompter days. Soup needs its moment, same as anyone.'

3: Panto week! Every dish is extra dramatic. The soup is doing a death scene with a borrowed lettuce. Encore at no extra cost.

stock.name: Singing Soup
stock.desc: She's shy today. Celestin has given her notes; she hits the high note for regulars only.

stock.name: Bowing Bread Roll
stock.desc: Please clap.

stock.name: Joke Pie
stock.desc: Tells a bad joke, free of charge.

stock.name: Dramatic Pudding
stock.desc: Dies on cue, eight shows a week, which is more than a bard automaton can manage.

interactables.name: Bertil Fjordhammer
pages: Furious Freja! Glorious Griefdom cuisine: porridge, black bread, smoked eel. Hearty, honest, and served with a scowl. The scowl's free.
Freja's my aunt. She came over from the Fiefdoms forty years ago with one pot and a grudge against the weather. The pot's in the back. The grudge is the menu.
My brother still writes from home. Since Trax fell it's Consul this, Consul that, and what can you say in a letter. I send him eel. Eel doesn't take sides.

3: I hear the Glorious Fiefdoms are showing face this season. Some of their lads might drop by. I'll scowl extra, then ask after my village.

brushoffs: *scowl* That's all there is. The scowl's still free.
Freja says buy something or move along. She said it loud enough that I only have to say it quietly.
FREJA! ...She's coming out of the back. You've time to run. Not to finish that sentence.

stock.name: Porridge
stock.desc: Served with a scowl. The scowl's free.

stock.name: Black Bread
stock.desc: Food for folk who've seen weather.

stock.name: Smoked Eel
stock.desc: Smoked the Fiefdoms way. Bertil has waited twenty years for someone to smile at it. Good eaters finish the eel.

stock.name: Mug of Something Hot
stock.desc: Freja won't say what's in it. Bertil has never asked. He drinks one at four every morning.

interactables.name: Zuzu Snapfilter
pages: Food blogger on Acorndr! Carna: five acorns. Goo to Go: one acorn. It ate my spoon, and I've had to post about grief.
She wiggles two fingers and steam curls back up off a cold dumpling. 'Minor illusion. I learned it for this. My parents paid for an alchemy degree.'
I quit the counting-house for this. Eight hundred followers. Mum checks every post and leaves the same comment: 'Are you eating properly?'
brushoffs: No new tea. My feed is all soup photos.
You're in my shot. Every shot. Bestie, please.
Blocking you. In real life. *turns around*

interactables.name: Lugg & Lissa Rivetbrow
pages: We've had our first date here, our wedding lunch, and our first fight. Over a Carna bun. We split it now.
Lugg's voting Rigrod. Lissa's voting Bosco, because his friends are in high places and she'd like one up there. We cancel each other out, then walk home holding hands.
Lissa wants a holiday in Wist, to hear real music played by real hands. Lugg wants this table, this bun, this Thoughtsday. Twelve years. We're saving for both.

interactables.name: Tabby Fusewick
pages: Lunch break! Twenty minutes. I work the cryston line at the plant. I've got fifteen minutes left. Fourteen.
The food court's the only place in Gok'Gok where everyone's equal. Equally queuing for Carna.
Since the moon moved, the coils on my line go strange at high moon. Sparks, a hum, and once a sort of note. Foreman says don't log it. I log it in my head.

4: Selunemas bonus at the plant! It's a hat. I'm wearing it. Mum got the same hat, same line, twenty years ago. She kept hers in a drawer.

interactables.name: Horbin Gleamtooth
pages: HO HO HO! I'm D'fain! Selune sent me! Have you been good? ...Don't answer, I can tell. Here's a candy cog.
This beard itches like a wool sock in summer. Don't tell the younglings. Selune's watching, and so's the floor manager. HO HO HO.
He wiggles his fingers and three snowflakes land on your sleeve, then melt. 'Took me two winters to get that right. The little ones think Selune does it.'
brushoffs: HO HO... you again? D'fain's list says you've had your cog.
Selune sees everything. Selune sees you coming back for thirds, friend.
Beard comes off in five minutes. After that I'm a goblin with a broom. Off you go.

interactables.name: Selunemas Tree
pages: A crystec Selunemas tree on the table, hung with glass cogs and tiny moons. At the top: Selune, with a little D'fain at her side.

interactables.name: Forgotten Notebook
pages: A notebook titled OPERATION SPORE PATROL. Sketches of a mushroom-shaped mall on a sea spire, purple stone, with notes in tiny writing.
'Their fountain has a fairy in it. Their stairs go up forever. Their soft pretzels are, sadly, excellent.' Signed only: 'A Cogskill Patriot.'

interactables.name: Food Court Bin
pages: A food court bin with three slots: RECYCLE, COMPOST, GOO. The GOO slot burps at you.

interactables.name: Napkin Dispenser
pages: A napkin dispenser that gives exactly one napkin, then a printed message: 'THINK OF THE TREES (MOFFIDGE HAS).'

interactables.name: Arena Overlook
pages: You lean on the railing and look straight down into the Mayor Klerp Memorial Arena. Tiny groundskeeper. Tiny broom.

0: From the overlook you can see the tryout targets laid out below: rails, chains and posts. Everyone's pointing.
1: Looking down at the arena: chalk lines, scuffs, and one target-shaped hole in the far wall.
4: Selunemas lights ring the arena rim below, blinking green and red. From up here it looks like a giant wreath.
6: Looking down at the quiet arena. Someone's chalked 'THANK YOU, TEAM' in huge letters on the floor.

interactables.name: Klerp-O-Scope
pages: A coin-op telescope bolted to the rail. One copper: you zoom in on the arena floor and read a lost button. It says 'BOSCO'.

interactables.name: Observation Deck Sign
pages: 214 OBSERVATION DECK · 215 ARENA OVERLOOK · 'Do not drop food on the brawlers. They have enough problems.'

interactables.name: Arena Stairs
pages: You take the arena-ring stairs down to the concourse.

interactables.name: Mister Mop
pages: *BEEP.* RESTROOM ATTENDANT UNIT. THESE FACILITIES ARE TWICE-FILTERED. PLEASE DO NOT WASH FISH IN THE BASINS. AGAIN.
*BEEP.* PLEASE DO NOT TOUCH THE VENT. GOOLAX PERSONNEL USE THE VENT. MISTER MOP DOES NOT ASK WHY.
*BEEP.* LOST ITEM REPORT: ONE MONOCLE. IF FOUND, RETURN TO THE THEATRE BALCONY.
brushoffs: *BEEP.* NO NEW DATA. MISTER MOP IS ALSO DISAPPOINTED.
*BEEP.* LOITERING DETECTED. PLEASE LOITER ELSEWHERE.
*BEEP.* SECURITY ALERT! ...MISTER MOP IS JOKING. MISTER MOP HAS A JOKE SETTING. SHOO.

interactables.name: Washroom Vent
pages: The vent grille has a gear-shaped keyhole. The brass key from the lift fits. *Click-whirr.* The grille swings in.
You squeeze into the duct. It's surprisingly clean, and smells faintly of Goolax coffee.
lockedPages: A vent grille with an odd gear-shaped keyhole. Warm air puffs out. Somewhere inside, a coffee machine gurgles.

hidden.hint: Warm air puffs from a seam in the washroom wall.

interactables.name: Pneumatic Tube Station
pages: A brass pneumatic tube terminal. A capsule rattles out into the tray. Inside, a memo on Goolax letterhead:
'ALL STAFF: Goolax liaison desk has MOVED. Ladder down to the service vestibule. Knock 3-1-2 on the gear door. Do NOT tell competitors.'
Below, in pencil: 'Unless they've come this far. Then fair play. — M.'

interactables.name: Service Ladder
pages: You climb down a long ladder into the dark... and land somewhere behind the arena concourse.

hidden.hint: A cold draught rises through a gap in the duct floor.

pages.text: You squeeze back out of the vent into the washroom. Mister Mop pretends not to see.
You squeeze back out of the vent into the washroom. The robot attendant pretends not to see.

interactables.name: Scratched Initials
pages: Scratched into the duct wall: dozens of initials and dates. 'G.R. yr 1'. 'TEAM COGSKILL yr 7'. 'I WAS HERE AND SO WAS THE COFFEE'.
Fifteen years of competitors who found the way. You resist the urge to add your own. Or don't.

hidden.hint: Scratches on the duct wall catch the light.

interactables.name: Dust Bunny
pages: A dust bunny the size of a cat. It blinks. It IS a cat: a clockwork cat, dusty and content. Its tag says 'BOLTS'.

pages.text: Bolts purrs like a tiny engine, then goes back to sleep on a warm pipe. So Rivets has a secret sibling.
Bolts purrs like a tiny engine, then goes back to sleep on a warm pipe. Somewhere below, you'd bet, there's another one.

interactables.name: Leyline Tube
pages: A long brass-and-glass tube runs the length of the room, humming and glowing faintly violet. The hatch reads: 'ONE RIDER AT A TIME. ELBOWS INSIDE THE LEYLINE.'

interactables.name: Ottoline Sparkvane (Leyline Operator)
pages: Welcome to the Leyline Operator! One rider at a time, straight down the leyline to Galleria Overlook. Mind the hum.
Fare's 50 gold for a round trip. You pay on the way out; the ride home is on the house. Hatch is at the end of the tube.
Side effects may include static hair, tasting purple, and a brief urge to hug a mushroom. All perfectly normal!
Galleria folk come out smelling of sea salt and moss, and ours come back the same. Thirty years I've run this tube. I've never once ridden it.
Goolax trialled an automaton operator in Reap. Lovely manners, couldn't hear the hum. One rider's hat arrived inside out. They rang me on Thoughtsday.
brushoffs: Tube's quiet, love. No new riders, no new news.
Hmmmm. That's the leyline telling you to come back tomorrow.
Any more questions and I'm charging you the fare. Off you pop.

interactables.name: Departures Board
pages: DEPARTURES: GALLERIA OVERLOOK, BANAÑON TOWN · ON TIME. Below it, a chalk line: 'MORE MALLS COMING SOON (PROBABLY)'.

interactables.name: Thessaly Reedmuir
pages: *hurdy-gurdy wheeze* Forty years I've played this plaza, friend. The gulls know every tune. Two of them sing harmony, and one of them is flat on purpose.
The theatre's got machines playing the music now. They never miss a note. Out here it's still just me and the weather, and the weather misses plenty.
Requests? I know 'Cog Me Maybe', 'The Harbour Waltz', and one about a crab I'm not allowed to play near children.
I was born in Wist. Left at nineteen with this and half a cheese. Now my sister writes that Tritone sings in the streets again. I'd like to hear it before I'm done.
brushoffs: That's all my tunes, friend. I'll learn a new one by next week, if my fingers allow.
Requests are closed. The gulls have booked the rest of the afternoon.
One more question and I'll play the crab song. Nobody wants the crab song.

interactables.name: Skiv Dampwhistle
pages: I'm on nights, but on days. Nobody can explain the rota. Mind the wet bit. All of it's the wet bit, sorry. I'm thorough.
The old maintenance gnome is training me. Thirty years he's been here. Me, three weeks. I've already got a favourite tile. Fourth from the fountain. It's got a fossil in it.
Arena days are the worst. Teeth, foam fingers, one shoe. Always one shoe. Where do the other shoes go? Is somebody hopping home every time?
Before this I gutted fish at the cannery on the docks. Nobody thanks you for a gutted fish. Here a lady said thank you for the floor. I went red all the way up.

interactables.name: Pemberly Coilsworth
pages: Just looking. I'm always just looking. Looking is free, and buying is how they get you. I've been not buying that lamp since Sew.
That Shimoto Scuttle costs more than my house. My house doesn't have six legs, mind. It hasn't got a door that shuts either.
I come in for the warm air and the floor. You can see yourself in it. My flat has one window and it looks at the gasworks.
Gran farmed barley outside Gok'Gok. She said everyone should own one beautiful useless thing. I'm saving for mine. Eleven silver and a shortlist.

interactables.name: Delphine Gearwhistle
pages: Morning laps! Twelve round the overlook before the shops open. Doctor's orders. Doctor is me.
Swing those elbows, dear! A brisk shopper is a healthy shopper. A slow shopper buys socks.
I've lapped that snail downstairs four times. He's very gracious about it.
There were nine of us once. The Gearwhistle Gallopers. Now it's me and whoever I can shame off a bench. I set bones for forty years, dear. A bench is a trap.

6: The bench dwarf did a lap! One! He stopped at every bolt he'd ever put in. Took two hours. Best lap of my life.

interactables.name: Orla Brassbuckle
pages: Sixty years I've had this seat. Sixty years of real players, sweating under real lights. Now? Pictures of machines.
Bard automatons, they call them. Write the tune, play the tune, never need a lunch break. Listen: every note's got a clank in it.
My grandniece finished bard school this year. Her whole class was meant to start work. The machines got the jobs. Not one of them hired.
My Dunstan played trombone in that pit thirty-one years. He'd wink up at me on the high bit and miss it, every time. I'd give a year to hear him miss it once more.

3: Real singers! Live! One cracked a high note and I've never been happier. I threw a rose. It hit the stagehand, and he said thank you. Lovely manners, that boy.
5: The pageant! Real people in a real panto horse; back half fell over twice. My grandniece is second fiddle in the pit. Sixty-one years in this seat, and I sat up straight.

interactables.name: Nim Quaverlight
pages: Third time this week! The brass ones play SO fast. No wrong notes, ever. I timed a solo with my pocket clock: forty-four seconds, every night, to the tick.
People say it sounds metallic. That's the BEST part. It's like music with armour on.
I want a little bard automaton for my room. Does Toggletec sell them? I'm going to ask Toggletec.
I play glockenspiel in the school band. Ms Fennick says I rush. The brass ones never rush. If I practise enough, maybe I'll stop being the one who's wrong.

3: Live opera's... fine. One of them breathed in the middle of a note. Breathed! The automatons never breathe. The old dwarf lady cried. I don't get it yet.
4: 'Deep Strait' has a crab in it. The crab has no music at all. I've been robbed.
5: The pageant horse fell over twice. I laughed so hard I missed the whole solo. Didn't even time it. Don't tell the old dwarf lady.

interactables.name: Corvin Ropeswell
pages: Stagehand, twenty-two years. Projector-hand this month, three shifts a week. I polish the crystal and wait for a cue. A picture doesn't need its curtain flown.
No sets to build, no wigs to find, no lead with a cold. Easiest month of my life. Worst month of my life.
I'll tell you a secret: I hum along with the machines, a bit flat. Just so there's one wrong note in the room.
He flicks two fingers and the little side curtain draws itself shut. 'Mage hand. Learned it for a quick change, years back. It's the only thing in here I still get to fly.'

3: Real cast this week! I've hung sixteen backdrops, lost a hammer in a tuba, and a lady in the front row hit me in the ear with a rose. Best week since spring.
4: Projection again, 'Deep Strait'. At night I rehearse the pageant with a broom as D'fain. The broom hits every mark. I've stopped mentioning that to the cast.
5: Pageant week. I haven't sat down since Meluday. If you see a moon on a stick, it's mine. Last year's went home with a dad in a D'fain hat.
6: 'Moons Over Toggleton'. Nothing to fly, so they let me lie on the floor with the patrons. Found my moon on a stick in the coat rack. It's staying under my arm.

interactables.name: Tesla Coil 'Sparky Jr.'
pages: A brass tesla coil crackles in a glass case. 'SPARKY JR. · Keeps your crystons charged and your hair upright.' Your hair agrees.

interactables.name: Personal Cryston Assistant
pages: A crystal cluster on a velvet stand. A card: 'PERSONAL CRYSTON ASSISTANT. ASK IT ANYTHING!' You ask the time. It hums: 'Buy now.'
You ask it the weather. The crystal glows a thoughtful blue and says, very clearly, 'Extended warranty.'
You ask it how it's feeling. It pauses. 'Shiny.' Fair enough.

interactables.name: Robo-Arm Demo
pages: A clockwork arm on a plinth offers you a handshake. Its grip dial is set to 'BRAWL'. You both let go at once. Mutual respect.
The sign: 'HELPING HAND 3000 · Stirs soup, holds ladders, waves goodbye. Does not do homework (anymore).'

interactables.name: Juniper Voltwhistle
pages: Demo staff. Watch: *presses button* ...Light comes on. Ta-da. I did three years under a lamp-wright in Beggle learning how that light works. Now I press it.
I've shown the Cryston Assistant forty times today. Forty people asked it something; it told all forty to buy it. None did. It's sulking, and it gets more breaks than me.
Don't touch the tesla coil. I mean, you can. But your eyebrows have to sign a waiver.
The demo bulb's dead. She glances at the counter, taps the glass, and a spark jumps from her nail. It glows. 'Don't tell the clerk. He'll want it every shift.'

interactables.name: Cryston Glow-Pet
pages: A crystal pet in a tiny cage. It glows brighter when you look at it. A tag: 'NEVER NEEDS FEEDING. NEEDS ATTENTION. CONSTANTLY.'
You look away. It dims, sadly. You look back. It practically explodes with joy. Twelve gold. You feel manipulated.

interactables.name: Wisteria Nodwhistle
pages: Land of Dreams Consulting Consortium, front desk. I keep the appointments, the biscuits and the nightmare ledger. Mind the ball pit. It isn't ours. The boy in it partly is.
Clients come in with a problem and leave with a solution. The bad dreams come later, as per the small print. I typed the small print. Smallest font we own.
I knit while I wait. Well, the needles knit. I hold the wool. This scarf is three years long. I'll stop when the ledger's full.

lines: Please hold applause till the end. Or the bit with the cannon. That's on your conscience.
Four hundred performances, and I still don't know who stole the cryston in act three.
Lost and found: three hats, a shoe and a very sad violin.
Pocket-Panes off, please. Acorndr off. Breathing on, but quietly.

lines: This coil's rated for ten thousand hours. Two thousand if you hum near it.
Warranty covers drops, spills and 'unexplained sparks'. Not explained ones.
A customer asked if crystons dream. I said only on commission, like me.
Mint is not lime. Please stop arguing with me about the Pocket-Pane.
Management wants me 'efficient'. I've been efficient since six. I'd like a sit by four.

2: Lor'Fida phone charm? Sure. It's a regular charm. We've told it about Lor'Fida.

lines: This cryston hums like a fridge. That one hums like a big fridge. I need a medium fridge.
My wife says 'just pick one'. Easy for her. She married me in under a minute.
Brightness, warmth, battery life... I'll come back tomorrow. I said that yesterday.
The clerk's stopped asking if I need help. We're like family now.
Hear that little catch in the hum? That coil won't see winter. Put it back.

1: Bought the lime-green Pocket-Pane. For the team. I regret nothing. I regret the colour.

lines: Wind-up frog's on special. It hops twice and then has a little think.
Everything in here goes 'boing', 'tick' or 'whirr'. The till goes 'ow'.
Please don't wind the display models. They get dizzy, and then they get ideas.
A youngling once wound the whole shelf at once. I still hear it at night.
No crystons in here, love. A spring never needs charging. Just a bit of faith.
Kids want glowing things now. I understand. I'd just like them to hold a spring once.

2: Unicorn figures are flying out. Kids keep asking why it won't eat the other toys.
6: Clearance! Mini-Brawlers half price. They still punch shins at full price.

lines: My quest is 'in progress'. I say that about my knitting too.

The clown on the flyer looks right at you. It isn't creepy. It's thorough.
Six years in this unit. Carpet still smells of juice boxes. I find it calming.

1: My consultant made the team! Read a book at a mimic, I hear. That's just good service.

lines: Shh. I'm hiding. From what? From dinner.
Found a sock in here. Not mine. It's mine now.
The balls are every colour except brown. Brown's a SECRET colour.
Ball pit rules: no grown-ups. ...Okay, you can stay. Be quiet.
The desk lady gave me a dream-safe biscuit. I dreamed about a biscuit.

lines: Folding jumpers is my cardio. Customers unfolding them is my weights.

Changing rooms on the left. The mirrors are honest. The lighting is on your side.

1: Everyone wants black now. We do 'very dark Soot'. For real black, go to Hex Topic.

lines: Grey or grey-brown? I'll know it when I feel it.

Mum says I dress like a chimney. Chimneys are very reliable, Mum.
They've moved the socks again. The mall wants me to walk past the jeans.

6: I bought the Smog. Decided in under an hour. The clerk shook my hand.

lines: Kettles in aisle four, aisle six, and the one we don't talk about in aisle nine.

Goolax stamped my crates, my counter, and very nearly me.

lines: Lord Clicks ate a broom today. Whole. He looked so proud I didn't have the heart.

lines: Today's the day I reach the food court. Or tomorrow's. I'm not fussy which.

My compliments to whoever mops. The floor is lovely and smooth.

lines: Selune for luck, Melune for nerve. Most brawlers buy both. Hedging is a faith too.

Quiet, please. The gentleman at the back is talking to his mother. Ten years gone.

lines: Newt eyes restocked. The newts are fine. They have little patches now.

Wizards haggle. Sorcerers don't. Warlocks just stare until I lower the price.

lines: Hexes left, charms right, Gerald in the middle, judging.

Return policy: you may return any cursed item. It may also return.

lines: Every edge honest. Some edges are rude. That's their right.

No swinging in the shop. Points down, pommels in, hands where I can see 'em.

lines: Browse. Wonder. Pay. In that order.
Everything here is exotic to someone. That is the beauty of it.
Don't tap the glass. The jar doesn't like it. Neither do I.
Haggling is welcome. Winning the haggle is not.
That gnome has bought four things he did not want. I respect him enormously.

lines: Is this a teapot or a helmet? The tag just says 'Yes'.

Every time I put something back, the dragonborn sighs. I've bought four things.
This lamp sneezes. Actually sneezes. He says that's a feature.
My daughter's coming Seluday to 'go through' my cupboards. I've hidden the lute.

4: Seven things bought since tryouts. Still no egg cup. I eat boiled eggs out of a helmet.

lines: Black isn't a colour. It's a commitment.
Piercings any day but Meluday. On Meluday we sulk, professionally.
That amulet's cursed to make you slightly cooler. Side effect: slightly colder.
Band tee restock: The Rusty Hinges, Soot Choir, and Melune & the Moodies.
The boss says our black is fading. I say 'vintage'. The boss says 'renovate'.
One kid asks for a darker black every day. I keep one back for him.

1: Everyone wants 'the Lightning Bolt special'. It's an earring. I made it up. It's selling.

lines: I asked for a darker black. They HAD one. This shop is incredible.
My new piercing whistles when it's windy. Gok'Gok is always windy.
I don't smile. My face does it sometimes. Without permission.
Black socks. Goth socks. Nobody sees them. I see them.
Soot Choir's playing the harbour on Wildsday. Mum says home by eight. EIGHT.

1: The owner signs things 'with eternal gloom' now. I wrote it on my arm. It's still there.

lines: Your aura's lovely. A bit smoky round the edges, but that's Gok'Gok for you.
The cards say 'patience'. The till says 'pay first'.
Selune waxing, Melune sulking in the wrong part of the sky. Great day for an impulse buy.
I can read your palm or your receipt. Receipts lie less.
Fae goods sometimes return themselves. Not to us. Just... somewhere.
My mother says fae charms are 'for taller people'. She owns three of mine, hidden.
Nobody asks for a reading on a good day. I try to remember that when they're rude.
Don't sniff the purple one. Or do. I'm not your mum. Read the label first.
Goolax potions taste like a coin. Ours taste like summer. I went through forty lemons.
That bubbling's normal. The humming isn't. Step back slowly. ...Lovely, it stopped.
Love potions are banned in Toggleton. Like potions are fine. They're mostly tea.
*waves a hand over a vial* Frosted. Poison. Right shelf, then. Good.

1: Hand-regrowth tonics are up four hundred percent. The medics bought six.

lines: Don't step on the fresh lines. They're chalk. I'm not.
I talk to Mayor Klerp's statue. Better company than most referees.
An arena floor's never clean. Just less dirty than it was last Seluday.
Found a monocle in the stands. Theatre's, maybe. The arena eats everything eventually.

lines: Arena walls: cold. Arena floor: sticky. Arena vibes: elite. Five acorns.

Best stream ever: twelve viewers. One was my mum. Two were also my mum.
Ring walk-around. Dramatic music, please. ...Anyone? Hum something.
That goblin by the fountain has two thousand followers. I've got twelve. Mine are loyal.

1: The unicorn eating that consultant has more acorns than my whole channel. I gave it four.

lines: Did you hear? Nubb from security had a second pudding. On shift. I only say what I hear.
Clara's Brews is out of Foundry Fizz. Or IS it? Somebody go and look for me.
The fortune teller said I'd meet someone tall. I'm a goblin. Everyone's tall.
I'm not nosy. I just stand near things that are happening.
Mum ran the gossip at the Pier Nine fish-weigh for thirty years. I'm the family business.
Nobody's ever told me a secret on purpose. I'd like that, once.

4: Selunemas is my season. Everyone's family's in town and nobody whispers quietly enough.

lines: Balcony's best for drama. Best for napping, too. I won't tell.
Lean back, not forward. Gravity has opinions.
I clap from up here so the actors think there's more of us.
Opera glasses for hire. A copper each. They're not a pair. One eye each.
The front-row lady hasn't mentioned her monocle once. She just squints at me.

5: Found the monocle. In my own coat pocket. Since week one. I need to sit down.

lines: Crystonade glows. Crystonade fizzes. Crystonade is not a cryston. Legal made me say that.
Salted beetle tip: chew during the loud songs.

Eleven years on this counter. I've heard 'just one more scoop' in four languages.
Popcorn's fresh. Fresh this morning. This morning counts.

lines: Clang is a good day. Clunk is a bad day. Clink, I've dropped an earring.
Bring 'em in dented, take 'em out dented less.
Mind the anvil. It's heavier than it looks, and it looks like a small cow.
Brannoc writes that the Practice Range has drums now. I've written back: good.
Stamp rent's due Seluday. I stamp a touch slower the day before, on principle.
Studs from the leather shop fall off and roll in here. I keep a jar by the quench tank.

2: Sand in your hinges? Bring 'em here. The Sloopermarket lot come in gritty as a beach.

lines: Lanyard? Lanyard. Everyone gets a lanyard. It's how I show love.

I have a clipboard for my clipboards. The top one's for emergencies.
Goolax gave me a whistle. Nobody said what for. I blow it anyway.
Mum asks what I do. I say 'events'. She says 'which ones'. I say 'all of them'.

lines: Cups, saucers, mugs, and a goat-shaped teapot. It pours from the nose.
Towels in Soot, Rust and 'Daring Cream'. I named Daring Cream. I stand by it.

Cushions fifteen percent off. Fifteen percent more cushion than you need, guaranteed.
The goo downstairs has been choosing that kettle for an hour. I've sent down a chair.

lines: Creak test! Bend your elbow. Hear that? That's quality. Or a draught.
Oil your leather weekly. Talk to it daily. Mine knows all about my sister.
A stud fell off? We'll add two more. That's our warranty.
People say it smells lovely in here. I'll have to take their word for it.
The smithy keeps a jar of our fallen studs. I'm saving up to buy them back.

lines: Nine hundred and one. I'm counting. I always count.
Cryston Crush took my last copper. I'm not mad. I'm just going to stare at it.
My thumb has a callus called Victory. It's my best friend.
Grown-ups play wrong. They read the instructions.
Sometimes the machine gives me a free go. It likes me. I've always known.

1: There's a Mall Brawl cabinet coming. Is there? I've decided there is.

lines: These leggings breathe better than I do, and I've been at it sixty-two years.
The fire elementals don't sweat in class. They just glow a bit brighter at you.
I miss the doilies. I don't miss dusting them.
Dolphin stretch number four. I'll let you know if I come back up.
The old fellow who laid this carpet tells me so every day. I'd miss him if he stopped.
No letter from my sister this week. The post from Quone's slow. That's all it is.

1: Class was packed this week. Everyone wants to throw a Bulwark now. We got a foam one.

lines: Third bolt from the left, that's mine. Sixty years. Still holding.
My knees and this bench have an understanding. Neither of us moves till lunch.
Pigeons come up here for crumbs. I come up here for the pigeons.
A lad came to count the benches. I said this one's taken. He counted me.
The lap lady reckons I'll walk by Selunemas. She's never met a bench like this one.

1: The Hex Topic gnome scorched a Breaker flat. Took me a week to build walls like that.
6: Did a lap. Stopped at all me bolts. Every one still holding. So am I.

lines: Foundry Fizz is a stout that thinks it's a soda. Nobody's told it.
Last orders is when I say. I haven't said. I'm enjoying the power.
Clara left one note in the till, years ago. 'More foam.' We're still working on it.
Water? This is a brewery. Fine. Here, with a lemon, so it feels included.
Me mam brewed on the barge with seawater. Whatever you do, don't.

2: I'm running a pool on the Sloopermarket. No money, just feelings. I've a lot riding on it.

lines: Order up! ...It's been up a while. It waited for you. Goo is patient.
Grey Goo's our classic. Greener Goo is our classic, but greener.
The spoons went missing in Sew. Straws only. I've stopped asking the goo.
A blogger gave us one acorn. I've read it eleven times. It reads kinder each time.
Gran said goo's for people who can't sit down to eat. That's most people now.

4: Selunemas Goo: red and green. Don't stir it. Leave it and it settles into a little tree.
6: A spoon came back. On the counter, with a note: 'sorry'. I've forgiven everyone.

lines: Meat's done when I say it's done. I've been saying it since nine this morning.

The grill's been on since the mall opened. Nobody knows where the switch is but me.
Big Bonk, extra bonk? That's a Bonk with a Bonk on it. We call that the Fortnight.
Mince went up with the rent. I kept the Bonk the same size and ate less of it myself.
The lad who checks my smoke gets paid in sausages. He's never short of friends.

1: New sign by the grill: MIND YOUR FINGERS. Tryout season. Someone always tries to help.

lines: Raw is fresh. Cured is patient. 'Just looked at' is for the brave.
Our fish are imported. Gok'Gok water's very... industrial. They're grateful.
Kelp comes free with every bowl. You don't have to eat it. The kelp will know.
Forks are by the till. I'd rather you didn't. Fish deserve fingers.
My grandmother's tide chart is useless since the moon moved. I keep it for the drawings.

2: Flot's team is Blue Tsunami. I'm not saying I'd cheer for them. I'd cheer near them.

lines: Squint all you like, the menu's mostly lettuce. Sorry, that was me squinting.
Our roots are local. Very local. I dug them up under the loading dock.
That plantling asks what's in the wrap every single day. Then he goes and gets noodles.
Mind the hole behind the counter. That's my break room.
Lent the pie shop a lettuce for a death scene. It came back with more attitude than me.

4: Selunemas Wreath Wrap! Yes, you can wear it. No, please don't wear it.

lines: The pie's forgotten its joke again and is improvising about the weather.
Soup, sing! ...She's shy today. Give her a moment and a little light.
The bread rolls bow when served. Please clap. They need it.
Every critic is welcome. Every critic gets the pie with the worst joke.
That automaton does eight voices. My soup does one, and you can have it with bread.

4: Back from the Panto trip, and the pie's got new material. Still bad. Well-travelled bad.

lines: *scowl* That one was free. So's the next one.
Porridge, black bread, smoked eel. Food for folk who've seen weather.
Freja's in the back. You can hear her from the leyline.
We don't do 'nice'. We do 'filling'. Filling's nicer than nice.
Back home we smoked eel on the roof. Here it's a box with a fan. Near enough.
Wist kids sing in my queue. Freja shushes them. I let them finish the verse.

lines: Five acorns for plating, two for taste, and one for a genuinely beautiful napkin.

lines.text: Aura Fist's judging rider leaked. Item nine: prison daddies, assorted. Five acorns.

lines: Lugg wants Carna. Lissa wants Whet. We get both and swap halfway.

lines: Eleven minutes. Ten if the Carna queue moves. Nine if it doesn't.

Foreman calls lunch 'an investment'. I'm investing in this bun.
Mum worked the line too. Ate at this table too. Different bun.

lines: *wheeze-twang* That's the harbour waltz. Or a gull. Hard to say.

lines: Wet floor! Wettest in Gok'Gok. I'm not bragging. I am a bit.
Left the sign by the stairs. Now it's a different wet floor, and I don't know where.
I mopped a snail's trail and he looked so hurt. I mop round snails now.
Somebody spilled Goo. The Goo's winning.
Mop, bucket, sign. The old fella says if you've got all three, you've got a job.

Projection! Bah. You can't throw a rose at light.
Forty young bards out of school, and the jingle in the loos wrote itself.

Foul! That's a foul.
I've got a whistle. It's imaginary. FWEEEP.
Pip's on a yellow card. His ninth yellow card.
No running near the noodles. It isn't a rule yet. I'm making it one now.

FISH!

Daddy, fish!

One more copper. The last one. ...Fine. The last last one.

I'm not with her.

Where does one get a snack for a bird? A large bird. With views.
Excuse me, what's a brawl? Everyone keeps saying it at me.
First time out of Banañon in eighty years. I keep touching the walls.
WHOOP WHOOP!
Knees up! Chin up! Rent... also up, sadly.
Hydrate! Lubricate! Dominate!
Nice form, citizen! You're not on the team? Doesn't matter. Nice form.
Clank-clank, that's my heart going. It's fine.
Who's got two thumbs and zero days off? *whirr* This coach.

Grade I in stock. Grade II coming soon.

Goolax: for whatever ails you!

Shine? Shine? I'm the shine.
Mind the puddle. I'm the puddle.
Pier Nine sends its regards. And its oil.
Bit of dock in your boots. That's character.
Born in a spill. Now I've got a job and a roof. Roof's nice.
The mop came by. I hid under the bench. The mop is not my friend.
*cough* Smoky enough.
Don't wave at me. I know what you're doing.
Grill's at 'perfect'. Perfect's my favourite smell.
They capped my chimney. Nobody capped me.
Paper hat's regulation. Grill lady gave it me. Never took it off.
Paid in sausages. Can't eat sausages. I keep them. I've got eleven.
Fold, fold, tuck. Fold, fold, tuck.
Not recycling! I'm staff! Look, a lanyard!
Damp today. Damp yesterday. Tomorrow I'm hoping for a bit less damp.
This box was my cousin. Rest well, Gerald-Two.
Sometimes I fold a box and it looks at me. Then it doesn't. Then it's just a box.
Gerald-One went to Moffidge on a cart. I wave at every cart now, in case.
*plink plonk* COG ME MAYBE, TAKE FORTY.
INTERVAL MUSIC. FOR THE INTERVAL OF YOUR LIFE.
MY KEYS ARE YELLOW. MY SPIRIT IS IVORY.
THE BRASS ONES NEVER MISS A NOTE. PLINKY MISSES THEM ON PURPOSE. FOR WARMTH.
PLINKY WAS LAST TUNED EIGHT YEARS AGO. PLINKY IS LISTENING HARD FOR SONG FORTY-TWO.
WELCOME TO COGSKILL ARCADE.
HELLO. YOU ARE MY FAVOURITE.
HAVE A CERTIFIED DAY.
BERTIE LIKES YOUR SHOES.
MIND THE PIGEON. THE PIGEON IS ALSO A SHOPPER.
BERTIE'S FIRST SHOPPER, OPENING DAY, WAS CRYING. BERTIE WAVED. BERTIE STILL WAVES.
Stretch and wobble, darlings!
I'm not melting, I'm relaxing.
Namaste. Na-ma-splat.
Breathe in through the nose. Or wherever you keep it. I move mine about.
Heated class is three silver now. I'm paying for heat I could make by standing still.
Someone in Glister still has a bit of my left side. I think about it on Wildsdays.
Lawn Wrap? LAWN?
Is that kale... Kevin?
Noodles. I'm getting noodles.
Lovely skylight. Good for my chlorophyll.
Aura Fist's very talented. The fans throw cut flowers at the stage, though, and I can't watch.
Somebody keeps watering me at the table. It's kind. It's also my lunch hour.
No hugs, please. A wave is plenty.
Water sparingly, the stars say. The stars have met me.
Ooh, a moonstone. Ooh, a price tag.
I'm prickly, not rude. The difference is about an inch.
I flowered once. Nobody was in. It was a Thoughtsday.
LOUDER!
Get on with it!
Bring back the cannon bit!
I've seen better from a pigeon!

Beetles. Beetles. Beetles.

Hush, dear.
Fifty years, same seat. I've outlasted four ushers and two roofs.
The interval is the best part. Gossip and biscuits, and nobody pretending.

Ambrose sat on my left for thirty years. I keep his seat for coats now.

lines.say: Granny Hesk! Say something ICONIC for my followers, babe.
Iconic. In my day that meant a saint on a plate. Step left, dear, you're in front of Gnorman.
Chat, she called me a saint on a plate. POSTING.
Tryouts in five days, Hesk! Who're you backing, bestie?
Whoever brings me a cushion, dear. The owners want rent on this bench now. I want comfort on it.
Hesk, that's BRIBERY. Chat, she's doing bribery.
That's Toggleton, dear.
Is it true the lizard boy fishes in there? With his face?
Babe, I've got eleven clips of him this week. Fishing's the only one I can post.
Well. Saves on bait.
Selunemas look, chat: TINSEL in the fountain. Hesk, thoughts?
The fish will eat it, dear.
Fish eating tinsel? Chat, that's CONTENT.
That's a vet bill. My grandson's beard cost less, and he's going as D'fain.
Brannoc, did you fix the loose board?
I respected the loose board.
That's not fixing.
Four hundred performances, Vimsy. That board has creaked on every cue. It is practically cast.
Someone asked if the balcony ghost costs extra.
We don't have a ghost.
I said 'not yet'. They bought two tickets.
I want a brawl musical. A big number for the Bulwark throw.
What rhymes with Bulwark?
...'Full work'? 'Pull. Work.'
We have no understudy, Vimsy. We have a crystal and a projection of a bassoon.
The back half of the reindeer-gear quit. Four shows a day was three too many, she said.
So the front half's on its own?
It won't stop prancing.
Then bill it as a solo.
Ozzle, love, does your dad know you're in the ball pit?
My dad thinks I'm at school.
And where's school?
Also the ball pit.
Mabsy, are you having the nightmares yet?
Just a small one. A clown with a clipboard.
Did it have nice handwriting?
...Actually, yes. Lovely loops.
The LoDCC man got eaten by a unicorn and came out FINE.
Came out of the unicorn, Ozzle. Let's not say which end.
I know which end.
Please don't.
My consultant says my quest is 'in the dream phase'.
That means asleep. Dad's in the dream phase every Thoughtsday.
...Has he got a consultant too, love?
Tibbet, could I leave some pamphlets on your desk?
Desk space is rented per pamphlet now.
That's corruption! I'm writing that down.
Four coppers a pamphlet, dear. I pay six a day for this stool, so you're on the friends rate.
The Bosco lad's giving out buttons by the range again.
We don't do buttons.
What do you do?
Honesty.
...Is there a button for that?
Excelsior wants a photo with the team.
So do the Bosco lot.
We won't bring buttons. We'll bring a clean count of the crowd!
Brawlers can't eat a count, dear. The Bosco lad brought nine hundred buttons and a tray of buns.
Snowflake pamphlets!
Same promises?
Same promises. Festive font. And a crossing outside the cryston farm, for my nephew.
Leave one. Not for the desk. For me.
Anything suspicious today, Tibbet?
A pigeon bought a map.
Did it pay?
Exact change.
Memo says I'm to smile at every customer now.
Can you?
I'm smiling right now, Nubb.
...Oh. Oh, Tibbet.
Fifteen people asked me where the lizard works.
Daranirn's. Unit 112.
I know. I'm asking how to make them stop asking.
Put up a sign.
Handbook page nineteen: signs. They read the sign, Tibbet. Then they ask me if the sign's right.
D'fain count?
Eleven so far. Two real beards.
Real D'fains?
Real beards. Grandads. One's been growing his since Reap and wants it on record.
Grub, you can't set up on the steps.
I'm not on the steps. I'm near the steps.
Handbook page thirty-one, Grub. Smoke counts as you.
Arrest my smoke, then.
Kebab, officer?
On duty.
Kebab, off-duty officer?
...In nine minutes. Keep one warm.
Tryout crowd ate me out of skewers.
Saw a fellow chanting 'Eat her leg!' with one of yours in each hand.
That's my chicken leg he was waving. Best advert I've had in six years.
Stalling next. Market folk, aren't they?
Heard they always finish with more people than they started with.
Like my queue. Starts with one gull, ends with half the harbour.
Is it always this... clanky here?
Clanky's our word for cosy.
Where are all the mushrooms?
Upstairs in the food court. In a broth. I wouldn't read the menu, dear.
Fifty gold, and my ears are still ringing.
That's the leyline saying hello. She likes you. She only buzzes the ears she likes.
Can it say goodbye?
Round trip, love. It'll say it on the way home.
I've come to see the scorch mark.
Arena's scrubbed it, love. Riders came through smelling of it for days.
All of it?
The groundskeeper kept a bit. Ask nicely.
Can I buy a ride as a Selunemas gift?
A ride. In a tube. Thirty years I've sent folk down it, and never once thought of it as a present.
My nan loves tubes.
...I'll make you a card.
If I buy the one that's 4% brighter, is it 4% less cheap?
...It'll be brighter.
I'll think about it.
You've been thinking about it since Reap.
Extended warranty?
How extended?
Until the mall's next owner.
So... a fortnight?
Do you sell the case Julip streamed the tryouts with?
That's just a regular case.
Is it lime green?
...It is now. Double price.
Selunemas present for someone?
A cryston. For my wife.
Which one?
Ask me again on the thirty-third.
Still the kettle, Snikkit?
Snikkit is listening to it.
It isn't on.
Snikkit is listening to its potential.
Does this kettle come in 'shiny'?
That IS the shiny one.
Shinier.
That's the price tag, love.
Twelve coolant cans sold today. Nobody in here owns a strider.
Snikkit bought two. For throwing.
Not in the store.
Snikkit will throw them in his heart.
Snikkit wants a Selunemas jumper.
Every one's got a cog on it.
Does one have a kettle on it?
Aisle nine. I'll ring it up with the kettle, love. Don't tell the till.
Gunnra! Your earplug's in my lane again.
Not mine. They come in ones.
Then whose ear is it from?
Ask the ear. Three hundred pairs sold this season, and every one came back a left.
Bosco button for your range, Sergeant?
If I pin it on a target, will folk aim better?
...Can I get back to you on that?
Practice bolts, sold out. You?
Lanes booked till Wildsday. Everybody's a sniper now.
Sigma Donk bought ninety.
And hit the crystal with one. Not bad.
BOSCO says he'd have made the team, easy!
Bosco's never hit a target in his life.
He IS a target! That's harder!
...That's fair, actually.
Ambrel, could you bless some newt eyes?
Well. Whatever for?
Premium line.
...Well. One blessing. Per newt.
Your sulphur's drifting into my incense again.
Call it a fragrance collab.
The gods are confused.
So are my customers. They're buying both.
Sold out of lightning components.
Sold out of luck candles.
Brawl's good for business.
Well. Folk used to come in for comfort. Now they want luck by the box.
Moon candles or D'fain candles for your window?
What's the difference?
One melts nicely.
The other one, then. I've had a week of nice.
Have you got this ring in a darker black?
That's our darkest.
Have you got it in sadder?
Back shelf. Bring tissues.
Piercing today?
Mum says no more holes.
Your mum's not here.
She's in Dullard's. She can sense holes.
Is it true the boss just blew on her hand after? Like a candle?
Like a candle.
I'm going to do that FOREVER.
You're going to burn your fingers forever.
Could you sign my tee 'with eternal gloom'?
The boss is at Coach Wire's practice.
Could YOU sign it?
'With moderate gloom. Vesper.'
...I'll take it.
What's this one?
A wonder.
What does it do? I've already got four things I didn't ask for.
It makes you wonder. Twelve gold.
Daranirn, is it true you've got a jar that laughs?
Everything here laughs at the right price.
That's not a no. I only say what I hear.
It's not a yes. Move along.
Is the hand for sale?
No.
Is it in the shop, though?
Also no. Buy an egg cup.
A judge called your lizard 'the real Toggleton spirit'!
He is not 'my lizard'. He is my employee, my doorman and my sign, in that order.
Same thing round here.
...He is going on the sign. In gold.
Lumi! Give my chat some gossip.
I don't gossip. I report.
Report, then.
Clara's Brews is watering the Fizz.
Chat's asking for a source. Chat is three people, and one of them's my mum.
Did you get the unicorn on stream?
I got the unicorn's back half.
The important half, then.
Don't.
Rumour for chat: Pocket Sand are all students.
Students! Then they'll be tired.
Or fearless. Poll's open, chat: tired or fearless?
Tired AND fearless. Worst kind.
Where's the finale? Give me a theory.
Somewhere with a lot of chairs.
That's every arena.
Then I'm right, aren't I.
Are those the targets? They look nervous.
They're targets. They're always nervous.
Poor things.
Don't get attached. I lost three at tryouts. Still say their numbers at lock-up.
Can I stand where the Breaker was?
You can stand where the scorch was.
Where's the scorch now?
Jar. In my locker. Tell no one.
Is that the statue he stood on? Mayor Klerp?
That's the mayor.
Did the mayor mind?
He's a statue, love. He was thrilled for the company.
It's so quiet in here between matches.
Away, home, away. Somebody keeps the lights on.
Do you talk to the targets?
No. They talk to me.
Mirabel! Still in there?
Still here, Spanner. Different shop, same carpet.
I laid that carpet.
We know, love, you tell us, and it's held up forty-one years, which is more than the doilies managed.
Has your Wrenna written? From the new Spangle's?
Says the new place gets nice light.
Tell her the snow globe misses her.
Tell the snow globe to write its own letter.
Our ambassador threw a Bulwark, Spanner. Eight points!
I built walls nobody could throw.
Has anyone tried?
...Don't you go giving her ideas.
Thermal leggings. Me. For Selunemas.
Sending my sister a pair too, love. She says the war's turned cold early.
I'll love them in private.
Wobbet, bestie, the followers are asking. Who IS Clara?
Couldn't tell you. Wages come in an envelope signed 'C.' Slurpa?
I met her... once.
And?!
It was fairly recent. Spring. I'm still... getting to the end of it.
Slurpa. Your goo ate my spoon. That was my CONTENT spoon.
It was... hungry.
It's FOOD, bestie. Food doesn't get hungry. One acorn.
That's... what you said... last time.
Coach Wire practised his 'whoop whoop' in here till closing. Had to frost him a glass to calm him.
I heard... most of it.
Everyone in Gok'Gok heard. It's trending on Acorndr.
He says the second whoop's still flat. Back tomorrow to fix it.
Selunemas drinks review, going live. Spiced Stout, Wobbet?
Like a hug from a barrel.
Three acorns. Mum's already commented 'too harsh'.
Barrels deserve four.
Big Bonk, quick as you can.
The Bonk takes the time it takes.
I've got nine minutes.
The Bonk knows.
Salad?
...Was that a joke?
First one in twelve years. Laugh.
Ha. Eight minutes.
Coach Wire wants practice after shifts.
Whose shift?
Everyone's. The plant lets out at ten. He'll be practising at midnight.
Then he'll be in here at one, oiling up next to my grill.
Our Selunemas bonus at the plant is a hat. Same hat Mum got.
Carna's is a bird stuffed in a bird.
Swap?
No.

...Bring it back alive.

In tune?

Sorry, sir! Sorry. I mopped your trail. Was that yours?
Ah. That's where I was.
Should I... un-mop it? Can you un-mop?
No, no. I'll make another. It's what I do instead of arriving.
Which way's the food court?
Up the stairs, round the ring. Five minutes.
For you.
...I'll bring you a bun.
Found another tooth by the arena. That's four this week.
Whose?
Lost property's. It's got a ticket now. Is that right? Sprocket said that's right.
Spanner! Up, dear! One lap!
I'm doing laps. In me head.
How many?
Forty. I'm exhausted.
You built these walls, Spanner. Walk past them.
Seen 'em. Bolted 'em. Sixty year and not one loose.
Your knees have three loose, dear. I can hear them from here.
So I sit by me walls. We hold each other up.
Hear that? Clank. Every single note.
That's the armour. They hit EVERY note. Ninety-four in that bar alone.
Music doesn't need armour, child. It needs lungs.
Lungs miss notes.
My Dunstan missed one a night for thirty-one years. I listened for it.
They wrote that whole piece themselves. No composer!
And no composer got paid.
My grandniece's whole bard class graduated this year. Not one hired. She plays weddings for soup.
Pass me a beetle.
You'll crunch over the solo!
Good. Somebody in here should make a mistake.
Brannoc, the projector wants polishing again.
It is a crystal, Corvin. It requires nothing of anyone.
It wants me to have something to do. I'm letting it.
Takings up eleven percent, Corvin. No wages for a cast.
No cast to take the bows, either.
The machines bow. Four shows a day, if the memo gets its way.
Same bow, Vimsy. Same angle, same beat. I used to fly the curtain for real ones.
Real actors back! One asked me where his trousers were.
Where, pray, were they?
Up the moon on a stick, stage left. I've no idea how.
Mum! When I'm big I'll brawl!
And I'll referee you. Foul number one: shouting.
THEN I'LL WIN!
Not if I say foul. That's foul two.
Nobody's brawling till the greens are... Pip. Pip, the gravy.
What do we say to the nice stall keeper?
MORE CHIPS.
We say thank you.
Thank you, MORE CHIPS.
Daddy, can I name a fish?
Go on, then.
BOLT! And that one's Bolt. And THAT one's...
...I think they're all called that already, love.
Lovely girl. How old?
FIVE.
Five! In my day five was old enough to... Forty years on this bench, dear, and now they want rent for it.
Rent on a bench? ...Course they do.
Birds ride free, but she has to sit still in the tube.
She did! Froze solid, like a mushroom after the first frost back home.
*fluffs up to twice her size and glares at the tube*
Still is still, love. The leyline doesn't mind a feather.
Do you have PikPiks in Gok'Gok?
We have pigeons. They have opinions.
*pecks the pillar, then pecks it again to check*
She thinks it's a tree. At home, everything's a tree.
Grill's smoky enough.
I didn't ask.
You pay me to tell you.
I pay you in sausages.
...Grill's PERFECT.
Customers say you make their eyes water.
That's the onions.
We don't do onions.
Then it's me. The chimney made eyes water. I'm keeping it up.
What's in the Lawn Wrap? Honestly.
Lawn.
Anyone... sentient?
Not since the incident.
I'm getting noodles.
Play the old intermission waltz, Plinky.
THE ONE WITH THE WRONG NOTE?
Especially the wrong note.
*plink... plonk.* FOR YOU, ORLA.
Plinky, can you play like the brass ones? They're FORTY percent faster.
NO.
Why NOT?
*plonk.* THEN NOBODY WOULD PLAY LIKE PLINKY.
OI! TIN-CAN! MISS A NOTE! GO ON!
THEY CANNOT HEAR YOU. THEY ARE LIGHT.
Then who's meant to shout back?
I WILL. YOU HAVE FOUR STARS. IS THAT ALLOWED.
Dad, why is that grandpa asleep?
He's resting his eyes, love. Like me after a night shift.
*snrk* ...Brenna? BRAVO!
He liked it!
Mum, is it the interval yet?
It started a minute ago. Sit on your hands.
Is it the interval NOW?
KID'S GOT THE RIGHT IDEA!

lures: Directions are free. Rumours are also free. Rumours are more popular.
Lean in, dear. The desk hears everything. The desk is nosy.
Got a minute? The desk has news. The stool has opinions.

pages: A sailor told me Blue Tsunami roll a whole wave into the arena in a barrel and pour it out at the bell. I asked who mops. He didn't know.
A trader off the tube says Stalling fight from behind market stalls. Every round more little vendors pour out. Flimsy things. One tap and they're down.
But they keep coming till the stalls are smashed. Leave them be and they nail the stalls back up. Hit the source, dear. The desk recommends it.
A pilgrim from New Zolvina asked for a quiet corner to chant. Says the B'dibom Bombs do the Holy Twins chant in matches. Two keep it going; the whole team heals a bit every round.
Break it and two of them lose a whole turn starting it again. So don't nibble, he said. Hit hard, all at once. Then he chanted at my stool. It squeaks less now.
Heard the Fairrest Federation forfeit if you put a rug down. Grass only, apparently. I've put a rug under the desk. Just in case.

lures: Psst! Come here. I'm not nosy, I'm just standing very near some news.
Did you hear? No? Oh, you've got to hear this.
I only say what I hear. Today I heard a LOT.

pages: Did you hear? The B'dibom Bombs actually explode. One per match. They bring spares. I only say what I hear.
Stalling's mascot is a goat that eats contracts. Goolax made them sign in iron this year. I only say what I hear.
My cousin's in Lor'Fida. The Broad Squad? Drag-queen monks! They fight in routines. Like a dance number, but with elbows.
And they huddle up close so they cover for each other. Harder to hit, and they hit harder. Pull them apart and the act falls over. I only say what I hear.
Ooh. The Glorious Fiefdoms cheat. Everyone says so. They bunch up in one big knot so the ref can't see the fouls inside.
Catch one at it and shout. LOUD. Make the ref look. Cousin says they could get chucked out of the whole contest. Scandal!
The Slymez stream their matches! Snailsmen. Viewers donate, and the coin buys them mystery boxes from the 'Cosmic Snailsmen Lootbox Service'.
Random magic battle stuff pops out, right mid-match. Mostly junk. Sometimes a LEGENDARY. I'd watch. I DO watch. Shh.

lures: The tube brings riders, and riders bring news. Want some?
Hmmmm. That's the leyline. And also gossip. Come closer.
Galleria folk talk the whole ride. I hear it all at the hatch.

pages: A Galleria rider swore No, But is an improv troupe. You must say 'yes, and', or you lose by default. She was tasting purple at the time, mind.
Ban'ton riders came over all bruised. Their next lot, Blue Tsunami, is all muscle. Barbarians, fighters, a couple of rogues.
Grab, shove, pin. That's the whole style, they say. Keep your distance and guard your soft ones. Like a cold leyline: don't let it hug you.
Monday's lot came back raving about the Broad Squad. Monks in full drag! They fight in routines, all sequins and kicks.
Bunched up, they cover for each other: harder to hit, and they hit harder. 'Split them up first,' a rider said. Then she hugged a mushroom. Normal!
A rider swears the Slymez are one enormous snail under a stack of hats, pretending to be a team. Clever, if true. It's probably not.

lures: Sit down, dear. I've news, and my knees want company.
In my day we gossiped to your face. Come here, face.
Old Gnorman, him on the fountain, always said I hear too much. He was right.

pages: The Broad Squad won't fight you till you compliment their outfits, I'm told. Well. Manners. I'd compliment them anyway, dear.
My nephew sells buttons at the Market. Stalling, dear: they fight from behind stalls. Out pop little vendors, more every round. Flimsy things. One poke each.
They keep coming till you smash the stalls. Leave them be and they build them back. Go for the stalls, dear, not the shopkeepers.
The Glorious Fiefdoms' captain is a duke, I'm told. Carried in on a chair. Mustn't touch the floor. I've a hip like that.
The Fairrest Federation, dear. Rangers and druids. Either they hang back in a long line shooting, or they bury you in animals.
Most turn into whatever beast they already look like. One stays a person to cast. Break the line and get to the back one. Old Gnorman on the fountain would've.

lures: Pull up a stool. The gossip's on tap tonight.
Barkeep hears everything. Barkeep repeats some of it.
Foam, ale or news? News is free. Ale is not.

pages: Market trader swears Stalling never pay for a round. They haggle the barkeep down to free. Not in MY bar.
Dock lads swear Pocket Sand's coach is a crab who only speaks in sea shanties. Fine coach, they say. Terrible tipper.
Sloppy Bottom Bay sailor in last night. Pocket Sand, he says: student wizards. They scratch runes on the floor. Burst, slow, push, even a little guard that pops up.
A rune nobody's set off yet can be scuffed out. Boot, sleeve, whatever. Read the floor and knock 'em off their concentration. Then he tipped in sand. Rude.
Trader says the Holy Rollers from Moffidge run screaming from garlic. Bring a clove, win a match. I've hung some over the taps. For luck.
The Holy Rollers from Moffidge came in for the stout. No captain, they said. Top of every round they vote on one target.
Anyone who hits that one does extra holy-light damage. Crossbows, silver, holy water, the lot. Whoever they pick, you guard. Paid in silver. Very polite.

lures: *BEEP.* MISTER MOP HAS OVERHEARD DATA. SHARING IS PERMITTED.
*BEEP.* RESTROOM ACOUSTICS: EXCELLENT. INFORMATION: AVAILABLE.
*BEEP.* PLEASE APPROACH FOR A FACILITIES UPDATE. AND OTHER UPDATES.

pages: *BEEP.* OVERHEARD AT BASIN 3: STALLING DELAY EVERY MATCH BY HAGGLING WITH THE REFEREE. MISTER MOP CANNOT VERIFY. MISTER MOP CANNOT HAGGLE.
*BEEP.* OVERHEARD, CUBICLE 2: POCKET SAND ARE STUDENT CASTERS. THEY DRAW RUNES ON THE FLOOR. BURST. SLOW. PUSH. ONE SMALL SENTINEL.
*BEEP.* AN UNTRIGGERED RUNE CAN BE SCUFFED OUT. MISTER MOP APPROVES OF SCUFFING. READ THE FLOOR. INTERRUPT THE CASTER.
*BEEP.* TWO VISITORS CHANTED IN STEREO AT THE BASINS. B'DIBOM BOMBS. THE HOLY TWINS CHANT. TWO KEEP IT GOING. WHOLE TEAM HEALS A LITTLE EACH ROUND.
*BEEP.* BREAK THE CHANT: TWO OF THEM SPEND A FULL TURN RESTARTING. RECOMMENDATION: BIG DAMAGE, ALL AT ONCE. SMALL DAMAGE IS LIKE SMALL MOPPING. POINTLESS.

lures: *scowl* Come here. Freja heard something, and she's furious about it.
News, with a scowl. Sit down, the porridge is still hot.
Griefdom folk talk over porridge. Loudly. I ladle and listen.

pages: Sailor at table four says Blue Tsunami train by wrestling icebergs. Lost twice. *scowl* Icebergs don't lose. That's what makes them icebergs.
*scowl* Glorious Fiefdoms. Freja's from up that way. She says they cheat. Bunch up in one big pile so the ref can't see the fouls.
Catch them at it and shout. Loud as Freja. They could be thrown out of the whole thing. She'd pay to see it. She wouldn't. But she'd scowl less.
The Holy Rollers from Moffidge ate here. Grim folk. No captain. Top of every round they vote on one target, and whoever hits it, it burns with holy light.
Crossbows, silver, holy water. Whoever they choose, stand in front of. *scowl* Good eaters, though. Finished the eel.

lures: OMG, come here. My feed is FULL of brawl tea.
Five acorns for this rumour. Want it? Free. Content is love.
My readers sent me something juicy. Not food, for once.

pages: My feed says the Broad Squad travel with a private brunch chef. Five acorns for the hollandaise. Probably fake. Very good photo, though.
A Panto foodie friend posted about No, But. Genasi! Each one floods the ground around them with their element. Fire, water, earth, air, lightning.
Standing in their own patch, they and that element's spells get the upper hand. So watch where you plant your feet. Two acorns for the fire one. Overcooked.
Have you seen the Slymez stream? Snailsmen! Chat donates, and the coin buys them random lootboxes. The 'Cosmic Snailsmen Lootbox Service'. Sponsored, obviously.
Random magic battle items, right in the match. Mostly duds. Sometimes LEGENDARY. Five acorns for drama. One for the lag.

lures: Psst. Buskers hear everything, friend. Folk talk right over the music.
Drop a copper, take a rumour. Fair trade.

pages: Market buskers say Stalling paid their entry fee in IOUs, and Goolax took them. I tried paying rent in IOUs. Didn't take.
Played the Market last spring. Stalling fight from behind their stalls. Little vendors pop out, more every round. One good knock each.
Smash the stalls and the flow stops. Leave 'em be and they nail the stalls back up. Aim for the timber, not the traders.

win: Boss. You won. I hung one black streamer. It's very festive. For us.
The till's been ringing since the match. I hate it. I love it. Mostly I hate loving it.
loss: We lost. Fitting. Black was always the colour for it.
Sit down, boss. I made tea. It's black too. What can I do?
none: Boss. Quiet week. I polished every amulet. One bit me. Normal Thoughtsday.

scrounge: I'll check the tip jar. And the cursed tip jar. Don't ask which is which.
research: I'll ask on the goth forums. We have forums. They're very dark. Someone always knows something.
gossip: Customers tell the piercer everything. Lucky for you, I'm the piercer.
tinker: Give it here. A little black polish, a little hex wax. Now it looks like it means it.

win: There's our ambassador! The fire elementals glowed so hard at the match, the studio's still warm.
Sales are up. I've sold leggings to a dwarf with no knees. What can I do for you, dear?
loss: Oh, dear. Come here. Dolphin stretch number four fixes most things. Cake fixes the rest.
I've put the kettle on. What do you need?
none: Morning, dear! Class is full, the leggings are folded, and I only cried once at the price tags.
What can I do for you?

scrounge: Let me check the lost-and-found. Yoga folk drop coins in downward dog.
research: I'll ask the fire elementals. They go everywhere and hear everything, then set it alight.
gossip: The front row hears all the gossip, dear. I AM the front row now.
tinker: I'll stitch it with the legging thread. Breathable! Stretchy! Possibly armour.

win: You won. Good. Customers stare at you now. Staring sells. Stand by the door and loom.
Before you loom: is there something you need?
loss: You lost. It happens to wonders too. Stand by the door anyway. Looming does not require winning.
none: Ah. My employee. The shelves are dusted, the jar is sulking, the prices are firm.

scrounge: There is a jar of loose coins under the counter. Some of it is even currency. Take what's fair.
research: I know traders from everywhere. I will ask. They will charge me. You will owe me one good loom.
gossip: Customers talk while they haggle. I listen while I win. Here is what they said.
tinker: Leave it with me. A little oil, a little polish, an 'exotic finish'. Same item. Better story.

win: Boss! The dream-phones haven't stopped. They're tin cans on string, but they ring in your sleep.
Three new clients signed. What can the front desk do for you?
loss: Rough match. I've filed it under 'Dream Phase'. Everything goes there eventually. Biscuit?
none: Morning, boss. Two new clients, one ball-pit youngling, and a nightmare ledger that's nearly full.

scrounge: I'll check the Consortium petty cash. It's a sock. A very thick sock.
research: I'll put out a dream-query. Someone, somewhere, will dream the answer. Then complain about it.
gossip: Clients talk in the waiting room. I knit loudly so they think I can't hear.
tinker: I'll leave it under the flyer press overnight. Comes out flatter, shinier and slightly haunted.

bastionTidbits.text: MALL BRAWL referees revive the fallen on the spot. Goolax pays the healers, which is why the healers smile so much.
All brawl gear must be homologated: a Goolax stamp on every blade, bow and boot. Unstamped kit gets turned away at the gate.
Every contest falls on a Seluday. Sixteen malls were announced; the banners now say twelve. Nobody's explained it.
The Sloopermarket's arena floor is all sand. Sweepers there are said to be very tired and very philosophical.
Immia Beach Mega Mall is in Lorfida, right by the sea. Sunnier than Gok'Gok. Everything is.
Goolax hands every competitor free healing potions each week. They taste like a coin, according to All Kimy.
The grand finale is on Selunemas. The venue is a Goolax secret. Even the groundskeepers don't know.
The Mayor Klerp Memorial Arena hosted MALL BRAWL's first year, fifteen years ago. A Year One coin still sits in the fountain.
Panto is a theatre town. Its troupes tour the malls; even Panto's Try's soup does a death scene.
Brawlers drink half price at Clara's Brews. Goolax pays the other half. Goolax may not know this yet.
Acorndr streams of every contest run live. The most-watched tryout clip was a target being scorched to soot.
